record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let Sα , 0 < α ≤ 1 be the subclass of S of functions f such that C \ f (D) is a single piecewise analytic slit from some finite point ω0 to ∞ that makes an angle at most απ/2 with the radii vectors. What can be said about the Taylor coefficients of functions in Sα ? If f (−1) = ∞ and f (eiφf ) = ω0 , −π < φ < π, find supf ∈Sα |φf |. (K. W. Lucas)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the standard class of functions
$$f(z)=z+a_2 z^2+a_3 z^3+\cdots$$
that are analytic and univalent on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For a parameter $\alpha$ with $0<\alpha\le 1$, let $S_\alpha\subset S$ be the subclass consisting of those $f\in S$ for which the complement $\mathbb{C}\setminus f(\mathbb{D})$ is a single piecewise-analytic slit running from some finite point $\omega_0\in\mathbb{C}$ to $\infty$, with the property that at every smooth point of the slit the tangent line makes an angle of at most $\alpha\pi/2$ with the radius vector from the origin to that point.

(a) Determine sharp bounds (or any nontrivial estimates) for the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of functions $f\in S_\alpha$, as functions of $n$ and $\alpha$.

(b) Suppose $f\in S_\alpha$ is normalized so that $f(-1)=\infty$ (i.e.\ the slit emanates from the boundary point $-1$) and $f(e^{i\varphi_f})=\omega_0$ for some $\varphi_f\in(-\pi,\pi)$, where $\omega_0$ is the finite tip of the slit. Determine
$$\sup_{f\in S_\alpha}|\varphi_f|.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any publication that resolves the coefficient problem or computes the supremum of $|\varphi_f|$ for the class $S_\alpha$ of slit mappings whose slit makes bounded angle with the radii vectors. No definitive evidence of a solution was found, so the status remains unverified.
